ceratocaudia:study:1.title: A new diminutive Jurassic neosauropod from the Kaladongar Formation (Khadir Uplift) of the Kachchh Basin, western India (Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, 2026)

facts.statement: The holotype of Ceratocaudia antiqua was collected from the Khadir Uplift of the Kaladongar Formation in the Kutch district of Gujarat, India.
facts.quote: The Ceratocaudia antiqua holotype specimen was collected from the low-energy estuarine sediments of the Khadir Uplift of Kaladongar Formation in Kutch district of Gujarat, India.

facts.statement: The genus name Ceratocaudia is derived from Greek and Latin words meaning 'horn' and 'tail', referring to a horn-like crest on the front tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The generic name, Ceratocaudia, comes from the Ancient Greek word κέρας, meaning horn, and the Latin word cauda, meaning tail, after the horn-like crest on the anterior caudal neural spine.

facts.statement: The holotype fossils are housed at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay in Mumbai, India, under accession numbers IITBR3–IITBR59.
facts.quote: They are housed in the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay in Mumbai, India, where they are permanently accessioned under as IITBR3–IITBR59.

facts.statement: Histological analysis and non-traumatic pathology suggest the holotype was an old, senescent individual.
facts.quote: Based on histological analysis and the presence of a non-traumatic pathology, the holotype appears to have been a senescent (old) individual.

facts.statement: Reconstructed muscle models suggest the tail of Ceratocaudia may have been used to deter predators.
facts.quote: A reconstructed muscle model of the tail suggests it could have been used to deter predators.

facts.statement: Ceratocaudia lived during the Jurassic period, specifically from the Pliensbachian to the Bajocian stages.
The time range for Ceratocaudia is estimated to be from the Hettangian to the Bajocian, between 201.4 and 168.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Bajocian (201.4 to 168.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Ceratocaudia lived in an environment containing abundant petrified wood and brackish-water bivalves such as Protocardia and Indocorbula.
facts.quote: The sediments in which Ceratocaudia was found also consist of abundant petrified wood and bivalves like Protocardia and Indocorbula that lived in brackish waters.

facts.statement: The coexistence of a large sauropod suggests niche partitioning with Ceratocaudia, though their specific ecological roles remain unknown due to the lack of cranial material.
facts.quote: The presence of a large contemporary sauropod suggests niche partitioning between it and Ceratocaudia, though it is unknown what ecological role they had in their environment, as both lack cranial material.

facts.statement: Ceratocaudia is classified as a macronarian sauropod.
Phylogenetic analyses place Ceratocaudia within Macronaria but outside Titanosauriformes, suggesting it is one of the oldest macronarians and indicating a global pre-Bajocian distribution.
facts.quote: Both analyses placed Ceratocaudia within the Macronaria, outside the Titanosauriformes, making it one of the oldest such sauropods and adding to the evidence of a global pre-Bajocian distribution of macronarians.

facts.statement: The parent group for Ceratocaudia is Macronaria.
Ceratocaudia belongs to the class Saurischia.
The genus Ceratocaudia contains only one species, C. antiqua, which is known from a partial skeleton.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Ceratocaudia antiqua, known from a partial skeleton.
